name: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
steps: Marinate chicken pieces in yogurt, half the ginger garlic paste, 1/2 tsp chilli powder and salt for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight in the fridge.
Grill, pan-sear or bake the marinated chicken until lightly charred at the edges and just cooked through, then set aside.
Heat 2 tbsp butter in a pan, add remaining ginger garlic paste and saute until the raw smell disappears.
Add tomato puree and cook on medium heat for 10-12 minutes until the oil separates from the masala.
Stir in remaining chilli powder, cashew paste and salt, then simmer for 5 minutes and blend to a smooth gravy if desired.
Return the gravy to the pan, add the cooked chicken pieces and simmer for 8-10 minutes so the chicken absorbs the flavours.
Lower the heat, swirl in cream, remaining butter and crushed kasuri methi, and simmer for 2 more minutes.
Finish with a sprinkle of garam masala and serve hot with naan or steamed rice.
tips: For an authentic smoky flavour, do a dhungar (charcoal smoking) step after the chicken is grilled.

name: Dal Makhani
steps: Soak urad dal and rajma together overnight in plenty of water.
Drain and pressure cook the dal and rajma with fresh water and salt for about 40-45 minutes until completely soft.
Heat butter in a heavy pan and saute chopped onions until golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for a minute, then add tomato puree and chilli powder.
Cook the masala until the fat separates, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the cooked dal along with its liquid, mash a few beans lightly for creaminess, and simmer on low heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in cream and a knob of butter towards the end and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Serve hot topped with a swirl of cream alongside naan or jeera rice.
tips: Longer, slower simmering on low heat gives the dal its signature velvety texture; do not rush this step.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
steps: Boil tomatoes and cashews together in a little water for 10 minutes until soft, then cool and blend into a smooth puree.
Heat butter in a pan and saute chopped onion until translucent, then add ginger garlic paste and cook briefly.
Pour in the tomato-cashew puree and cook on medium heat for 10 minutes until it thickens and the raw smell disappears.
Add chilli powder, salt and a splash of water to adjust consistency, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Gently slide in the paneer cubes and simmer for 4-5 minutes so they soak up the gravy.
Stir in cream, crushed kasuri methi and garam masala, then simmer for 2 more minutes.
Finish with a dollop of butter on top and serve hot with butter naan or rice.
tips: Lightly pan-frying the paneer cubes before adding to the gravy helps them hold their shape.

name: Shahi Paneer
steps: Boil sliced onions and cashews in water for 8-10 minutes until softened, then drain and blend into a smooth paste once cool.
Heat ghee in a pan, add cardamom and let it sizzle for a few seconds.
Add ginger garlic paste and saute until fragrant, then add the onion-cashew paste.
Cook the paste on low-medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until it turns light golden.
Whisk yogurt smooth and add it to the pan, stirring continuously to prevent curdling.
Add salt and a little water to loosen the gravy, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add paneer cubes and cream, and simmer gently for 4-5 minutes without letting it boil hard.
Serve hot garnished with a few strands of saffron or chopped nuts, with roti or pulao.
tips: Keep the flame low once cream and yogurt go in to avoid the gravy splitting.

name: Kadai Paneer
steps: Dry roast coriander seeds and dried red chillies until aromatic, cool, and coarsely crush into kadai masala.
Heat oil in a kadai and saute cubed onions and capsicum on high heat for 2-3 minutes until slightly charred but still crunchy; remove and set aside.
In the same pan add a little more oil, then ginger garlic paste and saute until fragrant.
Pour in tomato puree along with the crushed kadai masala and salt, and cook until the oil separates.
Return the onions and capsicum to the pan along with paneer cubes and toss gently to coat in the masala.
Cook for 3-4 minutes on medium heat so the flavours meld while keeping the vegetables crisp.
Sprinkle crushed kasuri methi, mix once more, and serve hot with roti or paratha.
tips: Cook the onions and capsicum on high heat for a short time only, so they stay crunchy rather than soggy.

name: Malai Kofta
steps: Mix grated paneer, mashed potato, cornflour and salt into a smooth, non-sticky dough.
Divide into balls, flatten each slightly, place a few cashews and raisins in the centre, and reshape into a smooth round kofta.
Heat oil and deep fry the koftas on medium heat until golden brown and firm; drain on paper towels.
Prepare a smooth, mildly spiced onion-tomato-cashew gravy as used for shahi paneer, and simmer it until thick.
Stir cream into the gravy and adjust salt, then keep the gravy warm but not boiling.
Just before serving, place the koftas in a serving dish and pour the hot gravy over them so they stay crisp longer.
Garnish with cream drizzle and chopped coriander, and serve immediately with naan.
tips: Add the koftas to the gravy only right before serving, otherwise they will turn soggy and may break.

name: Chana Masala
steps: Pressure cook soaked chickpeas with salt and enough water for about 20 minutes until soft.
Heat oil in a pan and saute chopped onions until golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for a minute, then add chopped tomatoes.
Cook the tomatoes down until mushy and the oil starts to separate.
Add chana masala powder and chilli powder, and cook the masala for 2-3 minutes.
Add the boiled chickpeas along with some of their cooking liquid and simmer for 12-15 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Lightly mash a few chickpeas to thicken the curry naturally, then adjust salt.
Garnish with chopped onion, ginger juliennes and coriander, and serve with bhature or rice.
tips: A tea bag or two added while boiling the chickpeas gives the classic dark colour seen in restaurants.

name: Rajma Masala
steps: Pressure cook soaked rajma with salt and water for 25-30 minutes until soft and tender.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped onion and saute until golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for a minute, then pour in tomato puree.
Cook the masala until thick and the oil separates, about 8-10 minutes.
Add chilli powder and cooked rajma along with its cooking liquid, then simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Mash a few beans against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy naturally.
Finish with garam masala, simmer for 2 more minutes, and serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Rajma tastes even better the next day as the flavours deepen overnight in the fridge.

name: Aloo Gobi
steps: Heat oil in a wide pan and add cumin seeds, letting them splutter.
Add julienned ginger and saute briefly, then add potato cubes and stir to coat in oil.
Cover and cook potatoes on medium-low heat for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add cauliflower florets, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt, and mix well.
Cover and cook on low heat for 12-15 minutes, stirring gently every few minutes, until vegetables are fork-tender but not mushy.
Uncover and cook for 2-3 minutes on medium heat to let excess moisture evaporate.
Garnish with chopped coriander and a squeeze of lemon, and serve with roti.
tips: Avoid over-stirring so the cauliflower florets keep their shape instead of breaking apart.

name: Palak Paneer
steps: Blanch spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, then immediately transfer to ice water to retain the green colour.
Blend the blanched spinach with green chillies into a smooth puree.
Heat oil or ghee in a pan, saute chopped onion until translucent, then add ginger garlic paste.
Add chopped tomato and cook until soft and mushy.
Pour in the spinach puree, add salt, and simmer for 5-7 minutes on low heat.
Add paneer cubes and simmer gently for 4-5 minutes so they absorb the flavours.
Stir in cream just before serving and give it one quick simmer.
Serve hot with a swirl of cream on top, alongside roti or rice.
tips: Blanching and ice-bathing the spinach is key to keeping the gravy vibrant green rather than dull.

name: Baingan Bharta
steps: Rub a little oil over the whole eggplant and roast it directly over an open flame or in a hot oven, turning occasionally, until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft, about 15-20 minutes.
Let it cool slightly, then peel off the charred skin and mash the smoky flesh with a fork.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped onion and green chillies, and saute until the onion turns golden.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook briefly, then add chopped tomatoes.
Cook until tomatoes turn soft and the oil separates from the masala.
Add the mashed eggplant and salt, mix well, and cook for 6-8 minutes on medium heat.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with roti.
tips: Open-flame roasting is essential for the authentic smoky flavour; grilling in the oven is a good substitute if needed.

name: Matar Paneer
steps: Heat oil in a pan and saute the onion puree until it turns light golden and loses its raw smell.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for a minute.
Pour in tomato puree, chilli powder and salt, and cook until the oil separates.
Add green peas along with a little water, cover and cook for 5-6 minutes until the peas are tender.
Gently add paneer cubes and simmer for 4-5 minutes.
Sprinkle garam masala, stir once, and simmer for another minute.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with roti or paratha.
tips: Frozen peas work perfectly well here and cook quickly, making this a fast weeknight curry.

name: Dum Aloo
steps: Boil baby potatoes until just fork-tender, then peel and prick each one lightly with a fork.
Shallow fry the potatoes in hot oil until golden brown on the outside, then drain and set aside.
In the same oil, saute onion paste until golden, then add ginger garlic paste and cook briefly.
Add tomato puree and cook until the fat separates from the masala.
Lower the heat, whisk in yogurt gradually while stirring continuously to prevent curdling.
Add chilli powder, salt and a little water, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fried potatoes, cover, and let it cook on low heat (dum) for 10-12 minutes so the flavours penetrate.
Sprinkle garam masala on top and serve hot with puri or paratha.
tips: Pricking the potatoes before frying helps the gravy seep in and flavour them from within.

name: Kadhi Pakora
steps: Make a smooth batter with half the gram flour, sliced onion, a pinch of salt and a splash of water; deep fry small spoonfuls into golden pakoras and set aside.
Whisk the yogurt with remaining gram flour, turmeric and about 4 cups of water until completely smooth and lump-free.
Pour the mixture into a pot and bring to a gentle boil, stirring frequently to prevent the gram flour from settling and burning.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the kadhi thickens slightly and loses its raw gram flour taste.
In a small pan, heat oil for tempering, add mustard and cumin seeds, dried red chillies and curry leaves, and let them splutter.
Pour the tempering over the simmering kadhi.
Add the fried pakoras to the kadhi 5 minutes before serving so they soften slightly but retain some bite.
Serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Using slightly sour, day-old yogurt gives the kadhi its characteristic tangy flavour.

name: Sarson ka Saag
steps: Wash all the greens thoroughly and boil them with green chillies and ginger in a little water until completely soft, about 20-25 minutes.
Cool slightly and blend or mash the greens coarsely, retaining some texture rather than a fully smooth puree.
Return the mixture to the pot, add maize flour mixed with a little water, and simmer for 10-15 minutes to thicken, stirring often.
In a separate pan, heat ghee and saute chopped onion until golden brown.
Pour the onion tempering over the saag and mix well, then simmer for a few more minutes.
Adjust salt and add a little more ghee on top before serving.
Serve hot with makki di roti and a dollop of white butter.
tips: The maize flour is essential both to thicken the saag and to round out its flavour; don't skip it.

name: Paneer Tikka
steps: Whisk yogurt with ginger garlic paste, chilli powder, gram flour, oil and salt into a smooth marinade.
Add paneer cubes, capsicum and onion to the marinade and toss gently to coat evenly.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Thread the marinated paneer and vegetables alternately onto skewers.
Grill on a hot griddle, tandoor, oven or open flame, turning occasionally, until lightly charred on all sides, about 10-12 minutes.
Sprinkle chaat masala and a squeeze of lemon juice over the hot tikkas.
Serve immediately with mint chutney and onion rings.
tips: Adding a spoon of oil to the marinade helps prevent the paneer from drying out while grilling.

name: Vegetable Pulao

ingredients.item: whole spices (bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom)

steps: Wash and soak basmati rice in water for 20 minutes, then drain well.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot, add whole spices and let them sizzle for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced onions and saute until light golden.
Add ginger garlic paste and mixed vegetables, and saute for 3-4 minutes.
Add the drained rice and gently toss to coat each grain in the ghee and spices without breaking it.
Pour in water in a 1:2 ratio of rice to water along with salt, and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on low heat for 15-18 minutes until the rice is fully cooked and fluffy, then let it rest for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
Serve hot with raita or a curry of choice.
tips: Soaking the rice and using a gentle hand when stirring keeps the grains long and separate rather than mushy.

name: Egg Curry
steps: Peel the boiled eggs, make a few shallow slits, and lightly shallow fry them in a little oil until golden in spots; set aside.
In the same pan, heat remaining oil and saute chopped onion until golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for a minute, then add chopped tomatoes.
Cook until tomatoes soften and the oil separates from the masala, about 8 minutes.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt, and cook the masala for 2-3 minutes.
Add about 1.5 cups of water and bring the gravy to a boil, then simmer for 8-10 minutes.
Add the fried eggs, halved or whole, and simmer for 5 more minutes so they absorb the gravy.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with rice or roti.
tips: Shallow frying the eggs first helps them hold together and adds a nice texture contrast.

name: Aloo Methi
steps: Wash the fenugreek leaves well, sprinkle with a little salt, let sit for 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess bitterness and water.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds, letting them splutter.
Add potato cubes, turmeric and salt, then cover and cook on low-medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Once potatoes are nearly tender, add the chopped fenugreek leaves and chilli powder.
Mix well, cover and cook for another 8-10 minutes until the potatoes are fully cooked and the greens have wilted down.
Uncover and cook for 2 more minutes on medium heat to dry off excess moisture.
Serve hot with roti or dal-rice.
tips: Salting and squeezing the fenugreek leaves before cooking removes much of their natural bitterness.

name: Kaju Curry (Kaju Masala)
steps: Soak cashews in warm water for 15 minutes to soften slightly, then drain.
Heat oil or ghee in a pan and lightly saute the cashews until pale golden; remove and set aside.
In the same pan, saute chopped onion until golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for a minute, then add tomato puree.
Cook until the masala thickens and oil separates, about 8-10 minutes.
Add chilli powder, salt and a little water, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the sauteed cashews and simmer gently for 5-6 minutes until they soften into the gravy but still hold their shape.
Stir in cream and garam masala, simmer for 2 more minutes, and serve hot with naan.
tips: Do not over-cook the cashews once added to the gravy, or they will turn mushy instead of creamy-firm.
